tool_input.command:
t=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$t/dest"
printf 'x\n' > "$t/dest/demo-20260101-120000.tar.gz"

bash rotate.sh --help > /dev/null; echo "rotate --help rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dest="$t/dest" --name=demo --keep=5 --quiet; echo "rotate =form rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep abc 2>/dev/null; echo "rotate bad keep rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --bogus 2>/dev/null; echo "rotate unknown opt rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --quiet -n --dest "$t/dest" --name demo --keep 0 2>/dev/null; echo "rotate keep 0 rc=$?"

printf 'deadbeef  missing.tar.gz\n' > "$t/dest/ghost.sha256"
bash verify.sh --dest "$t/dest" --quiet; echo "verify missing rc=$?"
bash verify.sh --dest="$t/dest" --name demo --quiet; echo "verify name filter rc=$?"
bash verify.sh -h > /dev/null; echo "verify --help rc=$?"
rm -rf "$t"

tool_input.description: Exercise rotate.sh and verify.sh flags after refactor
Remove probe script and show changed files

result:
Changed files: **lib/common.sh** (new), **rotate.sh**, **verify.sh**, **tests/run_tests.sh**.

Details:
- **rotate.sh** — the off-by-one: `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on an oldest-first list, so it deleted from the keep-th entry (the newest) onward and, at exactly N backups with `--keep N`, deleted one. It now deletes only the oldest `total - keep` files via `head -n` (with a guard for the `total == keep` case, since BSD `head` rejects `-n 0`). The inline option-parsing block and `resolve_dir` were removed in favor of sourcing the new `lib/common.sh`.
- **verify.sh** — sidecar parsing used `awk '{print $2}'`, truncating filenames at the first space; it now takes everything after the first whitespace run, and the digest comparison `[ $expected == $actual ]` became a quoted `[[ … ]]`. Same shared-code extraction to `lib/common.sh`.
- **lib/common.sh** — new, sourced only by rotate.sh and verify.sh (as instructed; backup/restore/report left untouched). It provides `is_uint`, `need_value`, `parse_common_options` (the full shared loop plus `--keep` validation, delegating unknown flags to each script's `parse_local_option`) and `resolve_dir`, with a double-source guard in the style of `lib/log.sh`.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — three new checks in existing style: verify reports `ok` for `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` (space in name), rotate `--keep 3` with exactly 3 archives deletes nothing and exits 0, and rotate `--keep 1` of 3 keeps the newest.

`bash tests/run_tests.sh` passes all 9 checks (`all tests passed`), and I separately verified both refactored scripts still accept every flag form (`--flag value`, `--flag=value`, `-q/-n/-h`, `--keep` validation, unknown-option rejection). One leftover: `/tmp/flag_probe.sh` (my throwaway flag probe) — deletion outside the repo was denied, feel free to delete it.
